tasks.short: Collect customer and item details and create an order draft.

steps.what: Receive the customer's order request and supporting information.
Find the customer account and check stored addresses and billing details.
Contact the customer for missing addresses, billing references or item specifications.
Enter customer details, product numbers, quantities and specifications into the order form.

loop.input: Customer order text or attachment, confirmed customer details and product catalogue.
loop.output: Order draft with field provenance and unresolved values.
loop.check: Validate schema, exact customer and item identifiers, units and quantities; never invent missing values.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; unresolved fields go to the order clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Unstructured requests need interpretation; structured form submissions use direct field mapping.

steps.what: Save the order draft and submit it for completeness review.

tasks.design: A configured intake form in the {WORKFLOW} collects missing factual details and reuses verified customer data from the {ERP}. An integration captures requests from the {EMAIL}; a bounded extraction loop prepares document orders for review, while structured submissions map directly into order drafts. The {ERP} queues saved drafts for completeness checking without releasing them for fulfilment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customers used different channels and formats, so clerks joined account records to free-text requests by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms and native imports already handle structured data. AI-assisted coding makes channel connections cheaper, and bounded extraction covers remaining document inputs.
tasks.still_hard: New customer identities, disputed billing changes and bespoke specifications require verification and conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a mistaken identity or specification before it becomes a confidently recorded order.

ambition.what: Provide a reusable repeat-order form for customers without electronic ordering connections.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time transcribing details and more time resolving account and specification exceptions. They gain no automatic right to change billing master data or accept unusual commercial terms.

reach.task: Create accurate customer accounts without duplicate records.
reach.learn: Customer matching, address validation and the evidence required for billing-detail changes.

evidence.claim: Order document capture can validate extracted information and post to the finance system.
Existing order software imports webshop orders and synchronises stock.
Validated forms and exact account matching can remove routine requests for missing factual details.

assumptions: The described intake route is email-led; phone requests remain an assisted alternative.
Standard factual questions can move to a customer form; inaccessible or ambiguous cases return to a person.
Billing information means invoice details and references; payment credentials use an approved payment channel.
An unmatched customer never triggers automatic account creation or a billing master-data change.
GDPR data minimisation, access control and retention apply to contact and billing details.
unknowns: Actual order-channel mix and customers' ability to use forms.
Customer identifiers available for reliable matching.
Verification policy for new accounts and billing-address changes.
Whether the {ERP} exposes draft-order interfaces and configurable forms.
Access approvals and employee consultation required under national rules.
research_questions: Which repeated order details could be prefilled from verified records?
Which requests require a conversation even after structured intake?
Does native import support preserve customer specifications and source references?
new_work: Handle customers who cannot complete the form.
Review extracted fields and unresolved account matches.
Maintain form fields, catalogue mappings and duplicate-detection rules.
Resolve failed imports and reconcile duplicate submissions.
Complete access reviews and applicable employee consultation.
tasks.statement: Obtain customers' names, addresses, and billing information, product numbers, and specifications of items to be purchased, and enter this information on order forms.

tasks.short: Prepare and issue invoices, shipping documents and contracts from approved order information.

steps.what: Collect approved order details, customer billing information and shipment confirmation.
Prepare the invoice and check prices, quantities, tax treatment and totals.
Prepare packing lists and shipping documents from shipment details.
Assemble the contract using approved templates and the agreed commercial terms.
Review departures from standard terms and approve or return the contract.
Post the validated invoice and send it to the billing contact.
Release checked shipping documents to the fulfilment team.
Send the approved contract for signature.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} to generate and release standard documents only after reconciliation and completeness checks pass. A deterministic generator fills approved contract templates from the {DOCS}; departures route through the {WORKFLOW} to the sales manager. The {ESIGN} receives only the approved contract version and verified recipients.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document preparation crossed several systems, and template changes were maintained separately from order data and approval records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document generation handles invoices and shipping forms. AI-assisted coding makes template mapping and approval integration cheaper; no model is needed to calculate totals or select approved clauses.
tasks.still_hard: Tax exceptions, specialist shipping requirements and negotiated clauses require expert resolution. A contract approval must remain bound to the exact version sent.
tasks.human_edge: Spot when apparently standard paperwork creates an unintended commercial commitment and obtain the right decision.

ambition.what: Pre-dispatch document-readiness checks for customers with complex billing requirements

tasks.altitude: The clerk focuses on transaction readiness and document exceptions instead of rekeying. The sales manager retains approval of nonstandard terms; no new signing authority is implied.

reach.task: Prepare a standard commercial offer with complete billing and service terms.
reach.learn: Approved clause choices, acceptance conditions and escalation limits.

evidence.claim: Order capture can validate customer, stock and price rules before posting order data.
Rule-based document generation and version-bound approvals are established implementation patterns.
The proposed document controls, time shares and build ranges are planning judgements, not a documented case outcome.

assumptions: The shares describe a blended workload; each order does not require all three document types.
The sales manager's approval time is included in task time and is not counted as order-clerk time saved.
Standard contracts use preapproved terms. Only departures require the approval step.
Failed billing or shipping checks block release and route to the responsible specialist.
Build ranges cover standard documents for one operating entity, access setup and applicable consultation effort under national rules.
unknowns: Which invoice formats, tax treatments and shipping documents are required.
Whether issued invoices and signed contracts have reliable correction and version histories.
Which terms require sales, finance or legal approval.
Whether the current {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ESIGN} support the required release controls.
Which document recipients and signatories are authorised.
research_questions: Can supported interfaces bind approval to an immutable contract version through signature dispatch?
How should partial shipments, credits and amended orders reconcile across generated documents?
new_work: Maintain approved templates, clause mappings and billing validations.
Resolve blocked transactions with finance, fulfilment or legal specialists.
Monitor failed document generation and signature dispatch.
Verify that released documents match approved data and versions.
tasks.statement: Prepare invoices, shipping documents, and contracts.

tasks.short: Tell customers prices, shipping dates and delays, and discuss delivery problems.

steps.what: Find the customer's order, agreed prices and delivery address.
Check shipment progress and confirm the latest supported delivery date.
Compose an update using confirmed prices, dates and delay information.
Send the update and retain the correspondence against the order.
Discuss serious delays and agree recovery options within delegated limits.

tasks.design: Join order details in the {ERP} to shipment events in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with freshness and recipient checks. Configure approved templates and event notifications through the {EMAIL}; missing dates, conflicting records and requests for concessions go to the order clerk. A recovery brief supports the human conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order and shipment records often lacked reliable links, and staff manually checked dates before copying them into messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing notification settings and modest integration code can cover routine updates. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort without improving unreliable shipment data.
tasks.still_hard: An expected shipment date may not support a delivery promise. Sensitive conversations, compensation and conflicting operational updates still need people.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise what a delay means to the customer and negotiate a credible recovery.

ambition.what: Proactive delivery-recovery calls before critical orders miss their promised date

tasks.altitude: More of the week goes to troubled deliveries and recovery conversations. Pricing, compensation and contractual approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Agree service recovery options with an existing customer.
reach.learn: Customer priorities, service commitments and concession limits.

evidence.claim: Integrated tools can answer order questions and perform supported order actions.
Order-management software can import orders and synchronise stock.
Templates and event rules can handle factual updates; time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: This describes a goods business with order records in the {ERP} and shipment records in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Routine messages repeat approved facts; they do not create new delivery guarantees or concessions.
Conditional recovery calls are averaged into today's task time. The communication channel shares differ from the weak mail prior.
Build ranges are working effort for one business unit. Access and consultation under national rules may add elapsed waiting time.
unknowns: Whether shipment events and delivery estimates are timely and distinguish confirmed dates from estimates.
Which customer contacts may receive each order's information.
Which commitments and concessions the order clerk may make.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed changes.
research_questions: Can the available interfaces distinguish dispatch estimates, carrier estimates and contractual delivery dates?
Which event and deduplication controls prevent contradictory or repeated customer messages?
new_work: Resolve stale or conflicting order and shipment records.
Maintain message templates, recipient rules and escalation thresholds.
Check failed sends and sample automated updates for accuracy.
tasks.statement: Inform customers by mail or telephone of order information, such as unit prices, shipping dates, and any anticipated delays.

tasks.short: Receive complaints, establish what happened, agree remedies and arrange follow-through.

steps.what: Register incoming complaints and link them to customers and orders.

loop.input: Complaint text and attachments, with customer and order lookup results.
loop.output: Complaint record with source references and unresolved fields.
loop.check: Validate identifiers against records; retain unmatched complaints without guessing their identity.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; unresolved fields enter the clerk's queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing forms handle structured submissions; free-text complaints require extracting facts from varied wording.

steps.what: Listen to the customer and clarify the problem and desired outcome.
Retrieve order terms, shipment events and previous contacts.
Ask the warehouse or service team to explain unresolved facts.
Choose a proposed remedy within delegated limits or seek an exception.
Explain the findings and proposed remedy to the customer.

loop.input: Verified findings, proposed remedy, approval limits and response template.
loop.output: Draft customer response with supporting record references.
loop.check: Check amounts and dates against records; clerk checks tone and commitments before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; disputed or sensitive exchanges return to a human conversation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover acknowledgements; explanations of disputed events require case-specific wording.

steps.what: Arrange the agreed credit, replacement or service correction and close the complaint.

tasks.design: Configure the {HELPDESK} to capture complaints from {EMAIL}, link evidence from the {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {CRM}, and route unanswered questions. A bounded loop drafts explanations; people handle difficult conversations and approve outgoing commitments and remedy instructions. The {WORKFLOW} routes remedies above delegated limits to the sales supervisor before release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complaint evidence spans several systems. Disputed facts and remedy negotiations resist fixed scripts.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case workflows and integrations cover routing and records. Bounded extraction and drafting reduce paperwork; AI-assisted coding can reduce connector development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Establishing responsibility, winning back trust and securing operational follow-through remain human work. Poor shipment records limit useful automation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the stated complaint hides a larger relationship problem and negotiate a credible remedy.

ambition.what: Weekly recurring-failure review with the fulfilment team

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time assembling evidence and chasing updates, with more time for difficult cases and recurring failures. Compensation limits and approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Review recurring complaints that threaten account retention.
reach.learn: Connect complaint patterns to account history, commercial exposure and practical recovery options.

evidence.claim: Knowledge-based answers, order lookups and escalation are available capabilities; negotiated remedies need separate controls.
Knowledge-based assistance can hand unresolved questions into a pre-filled request.
The step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured complaint outcomes.

assumptions: This baseline covers written complaints plus telephone clarification, with an existing case queue.
Relationship work remains substantial despite the supplied automation prior.
GDPR applies to customer data. Access design includes retention and role permissions.
Access estimates include assessment of consultation under national rules; formal consultation may extend elapsed time.
Any later automated customer-facing conversational service must meet applicable EU AI Act transparency obligations.
unknowns: Complaint volumes, channels and proportion requiring negotiation.
Available order, shipment and customer-history interfaces.
Delegated remedy limits and required supervisor approvals.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
research_questions: Which complaint categories can be resolved using existing records and approved remedies?
Does a case pilot reduce handling time without increasing repeat contacts or disputed commitments?
new_work: Review response drafts and unresolved customer or order matches.
Maintain remedy limits, routing rules and evidence mappings.
Monitor failed remedy instructions and reopened complaints.
Prepare the recurring-failure review.
tasks.statement: Receive and respond to customer complaints.

tasks.short: Verify customer details and order lines against source documents, master records and previous orders.

steps.what: Read the customer order and identify details requiring verification.

loop.input: Customer order text or attachment and its source identifier.
loop.output: Structured order details linked to source passages.
loop.check: Validate required fields, units and identifiers; flag ambiguous lines for clerk review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; unreadable or ambiguous orders go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use direct field mapping for structured orders; varied prose and document layouts need bounded extraction.

steps.what: Compare customer, address, product and quantity details with master records.
Check previous orders for duplicate references and inconsistent customer instructions.
Contact the customer to resolve missing details or conflicting instructions.
Confirm corrections and mark the order as verified.

tasks.design: Capture structured orders directly and use a bounded extraction loop for documents arriving through {EMAIL}. Deterministic checks compare fields with the {ERP} and {CRM}, detect duplicate references and show differences from previous orders. The clerk resolves uncertain instructions and approves corrections before the {ERP} marks the order verified.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order documents vary, while customer and product records sit in separate systems. Clerks compensate through repeated visual comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can produce structured fields with source references. Deterministic checks and a small exception screen can then handle most comparisons.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible historical match does not establish the customer's current intent. New delivery addresses, unusual units and conflicting instructions need clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a legitimate change from a mistake and obtain an unambiguous customer instruction.
tasks.altitude: The clerk reviews highlighted discrepancies instead of comparing every field. They can help customers remove recurring submission errors; authority to change customer master records remains unchanged.

reach.task: Agree clearer ordering arrangements with customers who submit recurring errors.
reach.learn: Customer purchasing processes, account communication and how to agree usable order templates.

evidence.claim: Document-based order capture can check customer, stock and price rules, route exceptions and post to finance records.
A vendor case reports 70% touchless orders at allnex; that result does not establish this customer's achievable rate.
Historical comparisons can use deterministic rules; ambiguity about customer intent still requires clarification.

assumptions: The baseline includes document-based orders; structured orders bypass extraction.
Historical checks flag field changes and duplicate references rather than interpreting arbitrary free-text instructions.
Order corrections do not silently update customer master records.
GDPR applies to customer data; source documents and extracted fields need controlled access and retention.
Access estimates include assessment of consultation under national rules where work practices change.
unknowns: Structured-order share and common document formats.
Customer and product identifier quality across the {ERP} and {CRM}.
Duplicate-order definitions and permitted tolerances.
Which changes require customer confirmation or specialist approval.
research_questions: Which discrepancies currently cause downstream fulfilment errors?
Can extraction preserve product codes, units and quantities reliably across representative order formats?

Maintain validation rules, unit mappings and duplicate checks.
Sample passed orders for missed discrepancies.
Help recurring-error customers improve their order formats.
tasks.statement: Verify customer and order information for correctness, checking it against previously obtained information as necessary.

tasks.short: Route approved orders to the departments that prepare and ship them.

steps.what: Check order approval, destination, stock allocation and dispatch requirements.
Resolve blocked releases, special handling or competing dispatch priorities.
Create preparation instructions identifying quantities, destination, handling and responsible department.
Email departments that the dispatch instruction is ready.
Check that the responsible department has accepted the preparation work.

tasks.design: Configure release checks in the {ERP} and route eligible orders into departmental queues in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Queue assignment replaces duplicate {EMAIL} notifications, while the {WORKFLOW} escalates unaccepted work. Blocked releases and competing priorities go to the shipping supervisor before instructions take effect.
tasks.previous_blocker: Release conditions and departmental responsibilities were inconsistently configured. Email compensated for gaps in queue ownership.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing release rules and work queues may already cover most cases. AI-assisted configuration and connector development reduce implementation effort without requiring a model at runtime.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting priorities, unusual destinations and special handling need clear operational authority.
tasks.human_edge: Balance urgent orders against capacity and understand when a technically valid release would disrupt operations.

ambition.what: Provide sales representatives with a pre-release split-shipment proposal for constrained orders.

tasks.altitude: The clerk monitors blocked and unaccepted work instead of repeatedly routing routine orders. They gain queue-triage responsibility; approval of exceptional releases stays with the shipping supervisor.

reach.task: Coordinate customer order priorities with available dispatch capacity.
reach.learn: Release cut-offs, warehouse capacity and the effect of split shipments on customer promises.

evidence.claim: Exact documents order imports and stock synchronisation, supporting structured order handoffs.
Configured release rules and departmental queues can handle routine preparation instructions without a model.
The estimated gain is greater than the human-heavy prior where orders are already approved and release rules are explicit.

assumptions: Most orders have structured quantities, destinations and handling requirements.
Exception discussion is averaged across the workload; not every order requires it.
The {OPS_SYSTEM} supports departmental queues and acceptance status.
Build ranges include permissions, rollout and assessment of consultation under national rules.

Can departments reliably work from assigned queues?
Which order categories require explicit release approval?
Do changed work allocation or monitoring arrangements require employee consultation?

Investigate orders stuck between assignment and acceptance.
Review exception reasons after operational changes.
tasks.statement: Direct specified departments or units to prepare and ship orders to designated locations.

tasks.short: Check requested products against stock, reservations and expected receipts.

steps.what: Read order lines and identify the requested product codes and quantities.
Look up physical stock by warehouse and stock status.
Check reservations, blocked stock and expected receipts to determine availability.
Ask the warehouse to resolve missing or contradictory stock information.
Record the availability result and unresolved shortages against the order.

tasks.design: Use existing availability rules in the {ERP} and stock feeds from the {OPS_SYSTEM} to populate each order automatically. Show stock status, reservations, expected receipts and data age together; route contradictions through the {WORKFLOW} to the warehouse. Keep inventory checks separate from stock reservation and customer delivery commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate stock and order screens require repeated lookups. Inconsistent reservation definitions and stale feeds undermine trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Standard availability configuration and stock interfaces often already exist. Small deterministic connectors and exception views can now be built with less development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Physical discrepancies, uncertain inbound dates and allocation disputes cannot be solved by reading records alone.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unreliable stock position and obtain a credible operational answer before anyone promises delivery.
tasks.altitude: Routine lookups largely leave the clerk's week; shortages and unreliable stock receive attention. The clerk can prepare substitution options, while allocation and delivery-promise rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Suggest commercially acceptable substitutes for unavailable products.
reach.learn: Product compatibility, customer constraints and the limits of substitution authority.

evidence.claim: Order import and stock synchronisation are available standard capabilities.
Order-processing systems can check stock rules and route exceptions.
Availability arithmetic needs deterministic rules rather than a model; effort ranges depend on existing interfaces.

assumptions: Product codes are already captured in the order; reading and re-keying them for stock queries can disappear.
A typical distributor has stock records in the {ERP} or {OPS_SYSTEM}; no spreadsheet bridge is assumed.
This task determines availability and does not reserve stock or send a delivery promise.
Access estimates include checking consultation under national rules where work practices change.
GDPR applies where order-linked customer information is accessed; the calculation itself needs only product and quantity data.
unknowns: Which system is authoritative for physical stock, reservations and receipts.
Feed latency and treatment of blocked, quarantined or consignment stock.
Existing availability configuration and interface access.
Frequency and handling time of stock discrepancies.
research_questions: Can existing availability configuration cover the required warehouses and stock statuses?
How closely do displayed availability results match subsequent warehouse confirmation?
new_work: Investigate stale feeds and contradictory stock statuses.
Maintain warehouse mappings and availability rules.
Review shortage alternatives with the sales team.
tasks.statement: Check inventory records to determine availability of requested merchandise.

tasks.short: Check order completeness and route missing information for follow-up.

steps.what: Gather the order draft and its supporting customer documents.
Compare customer documents with the draft's customer details, items, quantities and delivery instructions.

loop.input: Order review pack, customer record and product catalogue.
loop.output: Field differences with source references and unresolved item matches.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, units and quantities; require source references and flag ambiguous matches.
loop.stop: One comparison and one repair attempt; unresolved differences go to the order clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer documents contain varied wording and layouts; structured orders bypass the model.

steps.what: Check required fields and record missing or inconsistent information.
Ask the customer or account representative to clarify incomplete order details.
Assign the order to the appropriate processing or clarification queue.

tasks.design: An integration assembles each order review pack from the {EMAIL}, {DOCS} and {ERP}. A bounded comparison loop flags document differences; configured rules in the {ERP} check completeness and route orders. The {WORKFLOW} prepares field-specific clarification requests for the order clerk to approve before sending through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Required fields were often enforceable, but customer attachments, inconsistent item descriptions and disconnected queues still required manual comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing validation features cover structured checks. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records, while bounded document comparison handles variable wording.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting specifications, poor customer records and unclear responsibility for answering queries still need people.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when an apparently complete order still expresses an unclear or impractical customer requirement.

ambition.what: Review recurring missing-field causes weekly with the sales supervisor.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from checking every field to resolving conflicting instructions and recurring intake problems. The clerk can propose intake changes; approval of commercial exceptions stays with the authorised role.

reach.task: Reduce order delays caused by incomplete customer instructions.
reach.learn: Group clarification reasons and distinguish intake defects from product or commercial questions.

Required-field checks and queue routing usually need rules rather than autonomous agents.

Monitor integration failures and repeated clarification loops.

tasks.statement: Review orders for completeness according to reporting procedures and forward incomplete orders for further processing.

tasks.short: Sell relevant additional merchandise or services through calls and customer visits.

steps.what: Review account history, recent orders and open customer issues.
Check product information and select relevant additional offers.
Discuss needs, propose useful additions and respond to objections by phone.
Record the conversation outcome and schedule agreed follow-up.

loop.input: Clerk-written conversation notes and the permitted customer-record fields.
loop.output: Draft opportunity fields and follow-up actions with supporting note passages.
loop.check: Validate field types and dates; the clerk confirms intent, commitments and actions before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per conversation; unclear commitments remain blank for clerk completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes describe needs and commitments in varied language; fixed rules cannot reliably map them to fields.

steps.what: Approve proposed discounts or commitments outside the clerk's delegated authority.
Send the agreed offer or follow-up information to the customer.

tasks.design: The {CRM} assembles an account brief, and deterministic compatibility and eligibility rules produce an offer shortlist from approved information in the {DOCS}. The clerk conducts the conversation; a bounded loop converts their notes into reviewed {CRM} updates and follow-up tasks. An artefact generator prepares the customer offer in the {EMAIL}, with approval required for exceptional terms and for sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account preparation and follow-up span separate records, while customer conversations resist scripting. Reliable records still depend on the clerk completing paperwork.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured account views and small generators reduce preparation effort. A bounded extraction loop can turn the clerk's notes into editable records without recording calls.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, timing, objections and commercial judgement remain human work. Poor product compatibility data can make an apparently relevant suggestion unsuitable.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the customer's situation, recognise when selling would be unhelpful and negotiate within delegated authority.

ambition.what: Small repeat accounts receiving a scheduled replenishment call.

tasks.altitude: Preparation and paperwork shrink, leaving more time for useful customer conversations and planned follow-up. The clerk can prioritise eligible accounts within an agreed contact policy; pricing authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Develop a qualified additional-sales opportunity from a replenishment conversation.
reach.learn: Needs discovery, product compatibility, qualification and commercial boundaries.

reach.task: Summarise recurring objections for a proposed offer change.
reach.learn: Distinguish repeated evidence from isolated comments and assess margin implications.

evidence.claim: Account briefs, rule-based offer shortlists and template offers can reduce administrative work without automating the sales conversation.
The NBER study reports productivity gains from assistance in customer support; it does not establish additional-sales conversion gains.
GDPR Article 22 restricts certain solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.

The {CRM} exposes account history and customer issues sufficiently for an account brief.
Follow-up offers use standard templates, with explicit approval of exceptional terms.

GDPR and applicable national marketing rules govern contact selection, customer data and retention.

Handle missing account history and outdated product information.

tasks.short: Link incoming order documents to the correct record and retain a retrievable copy.

steps.what: Retrieve incoming order documents and attachments from the shared mailbox.
Match the document to the customer and sales order.

loop.input: Order document without a reliable machine-readable order reference.
loop.output: Candidate customer and order references with supporting source text.
loop.check: Require an existing unique order match, consistent customer identity and no duplicate document hash.
loop.stop: One extraction pass per document within a fixed input limit. Missing, conflicting or ambiguous references enter the review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use exact identifiers first. Varied free-text attachments sometimes require reading to locate the reference.

steps.what: Save the document with its order reference and retention classification.
Update the separate filing tracker so colleagues can find the copy.

tasks.design: Capture documents from the {EMAIL}, use exact references to link them to the {ERP}, and retain the original in the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop proposes references only when fixed parsing fails; the order clerk approves uncertain links before filing. Searchable order links replace the separate {SPREADSHEET} index.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent references and disconnected document storage made manual naming and parallel indexes convenient.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured capture, document hashes and record links handle most filing. Bounded extraction can recover references from varied documents without delegating record ownership.
tasks.still_hard: Duplicate customer records, amended orders and retention exceptions remain difficult. GDPR access, retention and deletion requirements must carry across the linked records.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve conflicting order histories and distinguish an amendment from a duplicate.
tasks.altitude: Routine filing largely disappears, leaving ambiguous references and record-quality checks. No new commercial decision rights follow from this change.

reach.task: Resolve duplicate customer records before linking new orders.
reach.learn: Customer identifiers, record provenance and controlled merge procedures.

evidence.claim: Order capture can read email and document orders, check rules and post to the finance system.
The allnex vendor case reports 70% touchless orders; this does not establish a filing savings rate here.
Exact matching, duplicate detection and configured retention can automate routine filing; estimates require validation.

A separate {SPREADSHEET} filing index exists in this representative workflow; companies with integrated attachments omit that step.
Human approval applies to uncertain proposed links. Exact unique matches bypass that review.
Build ranges cover one mailbox and archive, including access and any consultation effort required under national rules.

How often references are absent, reused or inconsistent.

tasks.short: Calculate merchandise, service and shipping charges using agreed prices and applicable rules.

steps.what: Retrieve agreed prices, discounts and customer charging terms.
Check shipment weight, destination, service level and applicable freight tariff.
Calculate line amounts, discounts, shipping, applicable taxes and the total.
Obtain approval for nonstandard discounts, freight waivers or unclear commercial terms.
Save final charges against the order for confirmation and invoicing.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} to apply versioned prices, discounts, tax rules and rounding rules, with shipment inputs supplied by the {OPS_SYSTEM}. The {WORKFLOW} holds only pricing exceptions for sales manager approval and records the decision before charges are saved. No model is needed for the arithmetic or rule application.
tasks.previous_blocker: The arithmetic is already available in standard software. Manual effort persists where freight inputs, negotiated terms or exception approvals are disconnected.
tasks.enabler_now: Configuration and deterministic integration can connect those inputs. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort without changing how charges are calculated.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear contract terms, missing freight dimensions and specialist tax questions need accountable owners. Existing standard automation may leave little additional saving.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a technically correct charge conflicts with the commercial agreement and seek the right exception.
tasks.altitude: Routine charge preparation largely disappears, leaving commercial exceptions and tariff maintenance. The clerk can propose corrections to recurring freight leakage; discount and tax decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Review recurring freight waivers and discount exceptions.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, customer terms and evidence needed to change charging policy.

evidence.claim: Order-processing systems can check price rules and route exceptions.
Charge arithmetic, rounding and tariff application are deterministic work when approved rules and inputs exist.
The implementation ranges assume reusable standard calculation functions and accessible freight inputs.

assumptions: The baseline uses existing calculation screens; it does not assume clerks manually perform all arithmetic.
Pricing exceptions consume a time-weighted share across orders and do not occur on every order.
Approved customer terms and applicable tax treatments can be represented as explicit rules.
This task saves charges; sending an offer, confirmation or invoice is a separate action.
GDPR applies to customer-linked data. Access estimates include assessment of consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which charges the {ERP} already calculates automatically.
Availability of versioned tariffs, contract prices and shipment dimensions.
Required tax, currency and rounding treatments.
Commercial approval limits and frequency of pricing exceptions.
research_questions: Can existing configuration remove the remaining manual calculation triggers?
Do representative standard and exception orders reproduce approved totals, including rounding and freight thresholds?
new_work: Maintain effective dates for prices, tariffs and charging rules.
Resolve missing shipment inputs and unrepresentable contract terms.
Check calculation changes against approved example orders.
Review recurring freight undercharges and exception patterns.
tasks.statement: Compute total charges for merchandise or services and shipping charges.

tasks.short: Trace delayed shipments and coordinate recovery with warehouse, sales, production and carriers.

steps.what: Check the order, promised date and customer requirements.
Check warehouse progress and carrier tracking for the latest shipment event.
Email the responsible team or carrier for missing shipment details.

loop.input: Order context, timestamped shipment events and the unresolved information gap.
loop.output: A short status request with shipment references and specific questions.
loop.check: Verify references and recipient; the clerk approves wording before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per request; missing references return to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template handles standard gaps; unusual shipment histories need a short contextual explanation.

steps.what: Discuss constraints and negotiate feasible recovery options with the responsible people.
Approve a recovery option requiring extra cost or changed shipping commitments.
Record the agreed recovery plan and next follow-up date against the order.

tasks.design: Combine order context from the {ERP} with timestamped events from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {PARTNER_PORTAL} in one exception view. A bounded drafting loop prepares unusual status requests in the {EMAIL}; people negotiate recovery and approve changed commitments. The {WORKFLOW} records the approved plan and schedules follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shipment references and event meanings differ across systems. Recovery also depends on people accepting changed priorities.
tasks.enabler_now: Available interfaces and configurable exception views can remove repeated lookups. AI coding can shorten connector development, while bounded drafting handles unusual explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Stale carrier events, missing scans and scarce production capacity. Software cannot make another team accept a recovery plan.
tasks.human_edge: Know whom to call, test whether a promise is credible and negotiate a workable compromise.

ambition.what: Reprioritise shipment recovery each morning and afternoon using verified delay and customer-impact signals.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time assembling status and more time resolving contested shipments. They can prioritise the recovery queue; spending and changed shipping commitments retain supervisor approval.

reach.task: Recommend which delayed customer orders deserve account-level intervention.
reach.learn: Customer commitments, account priorities and the commercial cost of delay.

evidence.claim: Joining order and shipment events by stable references can remove repeated status lookups.
Rossum documents order validation and exception routing; this supports order-context preparation, not autonomous shipment recovery.
Cross-team recovery negotiation remains dependent on operational constraints and human commitments.

assumptions: The typical setting has an {ERP}, an {OPS_SYSTEM} and carrier tracking through a {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Time shares are illustrative estimates, informed by the coordination-heavy priors.
Build ranges cover one order flow and a small carrier set, including access, rollout and consultation assessment.
GDPR applies to contact and shipment data; employee consultation depends on national rules and the proposed monitoring.
unknowns: Which carrier interfaces and stable shipment identifiers are available?
Who may approve extra freight cost or change a delivery commitment?
Does the proposed exception view require employee consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Which missing shipment events account for most follow-up effort?
Can configured exception views cover the main gaps before custom connectors are built?
new_work: Review drafted status requests before sending.
Investigate stale events and unmatched shipment references.
Maintain carrier mappings, escalation contacts and follow-up rules.
tasks.statement: Confer with production, sales, shipping, warehouse, or common carrier personnel to expedite or trace shipments.

tasks.short: Recommend suitable merchandise or services after understanding the customer's needs.

steps.what: Discuss the customer's intended use, constraints, preferences and budget.
Look up product specifications, service terms, prices and availability.
Compare suitable options and select a recommendation with relevant trade-offs.

loop.input: Customer needs and options already filtered against explicit constraints.
loop.output: Short recommendation brief with trade-offs, source references and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Recheck hard constraints and current prices; the clerk verifies suitability and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; uncertain suitability goes to a sales specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Needs and trade-offs are expressed in free text; fixed filters alone cannot explain their fit.

steps.what: Explain the recommendation, answer concerns and agree the customer's next step.
Record the recommended option and agreed next step.

tasks.design: A deterministic lookup combines catalogue, price and availability data from the {ERP} with approved guidance in the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares a sourced comparison for the clerk, who conducts the customer conversation. A configured template in the {CRM} records the selected option and next step after the clerk confirms them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information retrieval and recommendation judgement were mixed together, making the whole conversation appear resistant to automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Connected catalogue searches remove much of the lookup work. A bounded drafting loop can explain options using retrieved facts without taking over the customer discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Unspoken needs, technical compatibility, unreliable availability and consequential recommendations still require experience or specialist advice.
tasks.human_edge: Discovering what the customer actually needs and knowing when to challenge their initial request.

ambition.what: Offer structured option comparisons to occasional customers without a dedicated account representative.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more of the week discussing needs and trade-offs, with less catalogue searching. With training and explicit delegation, they can handle standard option comparisons while escalating technical and commercial exceptions.

reach.task: Assess compatibility for technically demanding customer requirements.
reach.learn: Recognise compatibility limits, capture intended use and identify when specialist validation is necessary.

reach.task: Follow up a recommendation with a suitable commercial offer.
reach.learn: Capture buying constraints and a useful next step without treating interest as a commitment.

evidence.claim: A shopping assistant for product advice exists; this does not prove suitability for technical recommendations.
An assistant study found higher support productivity, with larger gains for novices; recommendation quality needs separate testing.
Hard product constraints can be filtered deterministically before drafting an explanation.

assumptions: Current product facts and approved service terms are available from governed sources.
The clerk confirms outcome fields after the conversation; automatic call recording is unnecessary.
Recommendations stay within the clerk's existing competence and commercial authority.
GDPR applies to customer notes; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: How much of the catalogue has reliable compatibility attributes.
Which recommendations require specialist approval.
Freshness and reliability of price and availability data.
Whether the clerk has authority and training to serve occasional customers directly.
Applicable employee consultation and access requirements.
research_questions: Which explicit constraints eliminate unsuitable options without a model?
Can experienced clerks verify recommendation briefs quickly against approved sources?
Which recommendation errors require escalation rather than a revised draft?
new_work: Review recommendation briefs and confirm conversation outcomes.
Maintain suitability filters, source documents and escalation boundaries.
Check samples for unsupported claims and outdated product facts.
Train clerks to recognise technical limits and record unresolved needs.
tasks.statement: Recommend merchandise or services that will meet customers' needs.

tasks.short: Update inventory records from product movements and resolve unsupported adjustments.

steps.what: Retrieve recorded receipts, transfers, dispatches and returns.
Match movement references, quantities and units against current inventory records.
Ask warehouse personnel to explain missing or inconsistent movement evidence.
Approve a correction where normal movement evidence does not support the change.
Post validated movements and approved corrections to inventory.
Check that stock quantities agree with the corresponding financial inventory records.

tasks.design: Configure event-based stock posting in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, using unique movement references to prevent duplicate entries. A deterministic reconciliation compares quantities with the {ERP} and sends discrepancies to an exception queue. Unsupported corrections require inventory-controller approval before posting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Missing movement references, inconsistent units and disconnected stock records made automatic posting unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing stock-posting features and deterministic reconciliation cover the structured work. AI coding can speed mapping and validation development; no model is needed to calculate stock.
tasks.still_hard: Physical movement may differ from recorded movement. Historical errors, bundles, returns and unit conversions need reliable evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Establish what physically happened and distinguish a recording error from a real stock loss.

ambition.what: Prioritise same-day inventory discrepancies by their impact on open customer orders.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time posting movements and more time gathering evidence for stock exceptions. They can prioritise investigations; authority to approve unsupported stock corrections does not change.

reach.task: Check stock confidence before promising a rush-order delivery.
reach.learn: Available-to-promise quantities, inventory holds and the distinction between recorded and verified stock.

evidence.claim: Exact documents stock synchronisation alongside order management.
Reference-based duplicate checks, unit conversion and quantity reconciliation are deterministic operations.
Automating postings does not establish whether an unrecorded physical movement occurred.

assumptions: Routine product movements already create structured events in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
The financial inventory record is held separately in the {ERP}; a shared ledger would eliminate reconciliation.
Investigation and approval shares are workload averages across routine and exceptional movements.
Build ranges include access, stock-control validation, rollout and consultation assessment under national rules.
unknowns: Are stock and financial inventory already maintained in one ledger?
Which movements still rely on paper evidence?
Are movement identifiers, units and reversal rules consistent?
Who may approve stock corrections and at what thresholds?
research_questions: Can existing event-posting settings eliminate manual adjustments before adding an integration?
Which discrepancy categories most often block customer orders?
new_work: Monitor failed, duplicate and out-of-sequence events.
Maintain item mappings, unit conversions and reversal rules.
Investigate reconciliation exceptions and retain correction evidence.
tasks.statement: Adjust inventory records to reflect product movement.

tasks.short: Collect order payments, record receipts and forward any physical tender for processing.

steps.what: Send the customer an approved payment request with the order reference.
Check received funds against the payment request using settled bank transactions.
Resolve ambiguous allocations, short payments or unidentified receipts.
Record the receipt and allocate it to the order or invoice.
Send a receipt confirming the amount received and any remaining balance.
Where accepted, hand physical tender and its custody record to finance for processing.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} to issue payment requests and receipts from approved invoice data, and connect settled {BANK} transactions for deterministic matching. Exact matches post automatically; ambiguous allocations require finance approval. Physical tender retains a recorded human custody handoff where it is still accepted.
tasks.previous_blocker: Missing payment references, delayed bank imports and separate receipt records required repeated checks and rekeying.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured receipt workflows and bank interfaces can cover routine collection without a model. AI coding can reduce the effort needed for mapping, duplicate checks and exception views.
tasks.still_hard: Combined payments, partial settlements, unidentified senders and physical custody. Settlement and invoice allocation must remain distinct.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve disputed balances fairly and establish who paid for which obligation when references are ambiguous.

ambition.what: Prioritise unresolved receipts before each dispatch cut-off to prevent avoidable prepaid-order holds.

tasks.altitude: The clerk handles payment exceptions and customer explanations instead of copying receipts between screens. They can prioritise payment investigations; finance retains authority over ambiguous allocations.

reach.task: Help a first-time customer complete prepaid-order payment setup.
reach.learn: Customer identity checks, payment references, settlement timing and escalation routes.

evidence.claim: Structured payment-reference matching, duplicate detection and receipt generation can use deterministic rules.
Electronic payment evidence does not replace physical custody where physical tender remains accepted.
The human-heavy prior overstates routine handling where bank settlement and invoice references are structured.
GDPR applies where payment records contain personal data.

assumptions: Electronic payment predominates in this illustrative European setting; physical tender is a small conditional branch.
Time shares measure staff effort, excluding customer payment time and passive waiting.
Automatic matching requires a unique reference, consistent currency and amount, and no conflicting allocation.
Customer receipts use approved templates and confirmed postings; no model sees payment credentials.
Build ranges include restricted bank access, finance validation, rollout and consultation assessment under national rules.
unknowns: Which payment methods and physical instruments are actually accepted?
Does the {ERP} already provide bank matching and automatic receipts?
Which settlement events are authoritative for each payment method?
Who approves ambiguous allocations and payment-related order holds?
research_questions: What share of receipts can existing matching settings allocate uniquely?
Which payment exceptions cause the most avoidable dispatch delays?
new_work: Review unmatched receipts and conflicting allocations.
Monitor bank-import failures and duplicate receipt prevention.
Maintain matching rules, settlement mappings and receipt templates.
Retain physical custody records where needed.
tasks.statement: Collect payment for merchandise, record transactions, and send items, such as checks or money orders for further processing.

tasks.short: Inspect outgoing work against customer specifications and resolve discrepancies before release.

steps.what: Retrieve the approved customer specification and outgoing work documents.
Compare outgoing item codes, quantities and recorded attributes with the approved order.
Inspect outgoing goods for condition, finish, labels and customer-specific requirements.
Record discrepancies and recommend correction, acceptance or a dispatch hold.
Approve release or hold the outgoing work for correction.

tasks.design: An integration assembles the current specification and dispatch records from the {DOCS}, {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}. Deterministic checks compare recorded attributes and prefill an inspection checklist in the {OPS_SYSTEM}; people inspect physical work and judge discrepancies. The dispatch supervisor approves release, with findings and corrections retained against the order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications, dispatch records and inspection evidence were separate, while physical inspection could not be replaced by document checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations and checklist generators can now be built more cheaply. Existing structured attributes support deterministic comparison without requiring automated visual inspection.
tasks.still_hard: Surface defects, bespoke finishes, ambiguous tolerances and unrecorded changes still require physical assessment and specialist judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a defect or mismatch that passes the recorded checks and deciding its practical significance.

ambition.what: Review recurring specification mismatches weekly with the sales supervisor.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time assembling paperwork and more time inspecting work and documenting consequential discrepancies. Dispatch approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Prevent repeat order errors caused by unclear customer promises.
reach.learn: Translate inspection findings into precise order-entry requirements and customer acceptance criteria.

reach.task: Clarify technical acceptance criteria before an order is fulfilled.
reach.learn: Distinguish measurable tolerances from subjective preferences and identify authoritative specification versions.

evidence.claim: Order software can synchronise order and stock records; this does not establish physical inspection automation.
Recorded item codes, quantities and explicit tolerances can be compared deterministically.
Physical condition and ambiguous customer acceptance criteria commonly require human inspection.

assumptions: This version describes a merchandise business where the order clerk inspects outgoing goods.
Physical inspection takes more time than the supplied document-heavy prior suggests.
A dispatch supervisor currently approves release; local authority arrangements may differ.
Only approved structured criteria generate automatic checks; novel free-text requirements receive human interpretation.
GDPR applies to identifiable customer and employee records; consultation follows national rules.
unknowns: Whether outgoing work consists of goods, service deliverables or advertising proofs.
Who performs physical inspection and who has release authority.
Which specification attributes and tolerances are structured.
How specification revisions and customer-approved deviations are recorded.
Whether suitable checklists already exist in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Access lead times and applicable employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which checks compare records, and which require observing the actual outgoing work?
Can the authoritative specification version be linked reliably to each dispatch?
Which discrepancy types recur and could be prevented during order intake?
new_work: Maintain checklist templates and approved tolerance rules.
Translate new customer-specific conditions into inspection criteria.
Resolve missing or conflicting specification versions.
Review comparison failures and maintain integration mappings.
Complete employee consultation where national rules require it.
tasks.statement: Inspect outgoing work for compliance with customers' specifications.

tasks.short: Warn relevant teams when stock is low or incoming orders threaten available supply.

steps.what: Check stock on hand, reservations and expected receipts.
Compare open order demand with available supply and shortage thresholds.
Assess uncertain shortages and identify affected commitments and urgency.
Notify purchasing and fulfilment teams with affected items, orders and required dates.
Check acknowledgement and remind the responsible team about unresolved shortages.

tasks.design: Calculate time-phased available supply from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and open demand in the {ERP}, using existing shortage alerts where sufficient. A {WORKFLOW} routes deduplicated notices through the {EMAIL} and tracks acknowledgement. A {BI} view prepares uncertain shortages for human assessment without allocating stock or placing purchases.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock, reservations and open demand were checked on different screens, while notices and follow-up lacked a shared case identifier.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing stock alerts cover simple thresholds. Small integrations can add time-phased comparisons, recipient routing and acknowledgement tracking.
tasks.still_hard: Inventory accuracy and receipt reliability determine alert quality. Deciding which customer commitment takes priority remains a commercial and operational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when apparently sufficient stock is unusable, uncertain or already informally committed.

ambition.what: Daily delivery-risk triage with purchasing and fulfilment

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time chasing acknowledgements and more time explaining threatened commitments. Stock allocation and purchasing authority remain with the responsible teams.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of non-retail sales workers
reach.task: Recommend which threatened customer commitments require escalation.
reach.learn: Service priorities, stock reservation rules and replenishment constraints.

evidence.claim: Order-management software supports stock synchronisation, providing part of the required data foundation.
Time-phased shortage calculations, routing and acknowledgement tracking can use deterministic rules.
Today's shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The {SPREADSHEET} is used for cross-system shortage assessment, rather than as the stock ledger.
Notifications stay internal, despite the prior suggesting external action. Purchase orders and customer promises are outside this task.
Routine threshold breaches bypass human assessment; uncertain shortages receive it.
Build ranges include access setup and applicable consultation effort under national rules; approval waiting time is additional.
unknowns: Whether reservations, receipts and demand use compatible dates, units and item identifiers.
Which shortages require immediate escalation rather than a digest.
Who owns acknowledgement and resolution for each item category.
Whether existing stock alerts already cover the required calculation.
research_questions: Can the supported interfaces expose reservation changes without double-counting committed demand?
Which alert suppression rules reduce repeats while preserving material changes in shortage severity?
new_work: Maintain thresholds, routing and escalation timers.
Investigate stale inventory feeds and unreliable receipt dates.
Review repeated alerts and unresolved shortage cases.
tasks.statement: Notify departments when supplies of specific items are low, or when orders would deplete available supplies.

tasks.short: Recommend suitable packing and labels for customer orders.

steps.what: Check ordered items, quantities, destination and recorded handling requirements.
Read customer packing instructions and applicable packing specifications.

loop.input: Customer instructions and the current packing specifications.
loop.output: Structured packing requirements with source passages and unresolved conflicts.
loop.check: Validate required fields, units and document versions; the clerk confirms extracted requirements before use.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per instruction pack; unresolved or missing requirements go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer instructions contain varied prose, exceptions and document layouts that fixed field mappings cannot reliably capture.

steps.what: Select a packing method and label specification against the requirements.
Resolve nonstandard requirements and approve exceptional packing arrangements.
Record packing and label instructions on the order for fulfilment.

tasks.design: The {ERP} supplies item and destination attributes, while a bounded extraction loop turns instructions in the {DOCS} into requirements for clerk review. Versioned rules in the {WORKFLOW} select standard packing and labels; unmatched or conflicting requirements go to the warehouse supervisor. Only rule-covered recommendations or approved exception plans become packing instructions in the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Packing knowledge is split between specifications, customer instructions and warehouse experience. Incomplete item attributes prevent reliable rule matching.
tasks.enabler_now: A small extraction loop can prepare free-text requirements, while ordinary rules handle known combinations. Existing order fields and approval configuration can carry the result.
tasks.still_hard: Physical condition, unusual loads and safety-critical shipments need qualified judgement. Extraction cannot establish that a packing method is safe or legally sufficient.
tasks.human_edge: Notice unusual handling risks, question conflicting instructions and involve qualified specialists when needed.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time searching specifications and retyping instructions, and more time resolving unusual requirements with fulfilment staff. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Clarify customer handling requirements before an order is accepted.
reach.learn: Packing constraints, label requirements and when to seek warehouse or specialist advice.

evidence.claim: Standard packing choices can use versioned decision tables when item and shipment attributes are complete.
Rossum documents extraction from order documents, business-rule checks and exception routing; this supports the capture pattern, not packing safety.

assumptions: The workflow covers ordinary merchandise; specialist shipments are routed to qualified people.
Approved packing rules exist or can be documented before automated selection starts.
Time shares are averaged across routine orders and orders requiring consultation.
Build ranges include access approval and a national consultation check; they exclude developing specialist packing standards.
Customer documents receive purpose-limited access and retention under GDPR.
unknowns: Completeness of item dimensions, weights and handling classifications.
Which packing standards and destination requirements apply.
Who is qualified to approve safety-critical or nonstandard arrangements.
Whether the {ERP} can enforce unresolved-exception holds.
research_questions: Which requirements can be expressed as complete, testable rules?
What test set covers conflicting instructions, missing attributes and obsolete specifications?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and resolve ambiguous passages.
Maintain packing rules, specification versions and specialist escalation routes.
Investigate incorrect recommendations and update the regression examples.
tasks.statement: Recommend type of packing or labeling needed on order.

tasks.short: Compile order statistics and prepare management reports.

steps.what: Export orders, cancellations and order values for the reporting period.
Retrieve shipment dates and outstanding quantities.
Match exports, resolve discrepancies and calculate agreed order statistics.
Prepare the management report and explain material changes.
Email the report to management and retain the distributed version.

tasks.design: Scheduled exports from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} feed deterministic joins, reconciliations and calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. An artefact generator prepares tables and threshold-based variance statements; the order clerk resolves exceptions and adds explanations before publishing an approved snapshot in the {BI}. Management reads the shared snapshot, removing attachment distribution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate exports, inconsistent order identifiers and changing metric definitions make a recurring report costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and reporting features can cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building missing joins, checks and report templates; no model is needed at runtime.
tasks.still_hard: Partial deliveries, returns, currency changes and reporting cut-offs can change the meaning of a metric. Explaining causes still needs operational knowledge.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparent sales change is a data issue, and explain which operational action management should consider.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of overdue order exceptions instead of waiting for the management reporting cycle.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling reports to investigating exceptions and proposing order-recovery priorities. Commercial and fulfilment approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare an evidence-based order-recovery priority list.
reach.learn: Backlog ageing, margin interpretation and the limits of order-value measures.

evidence.claim: Fixed order metrics, reconciliation checks and report templates can use deterministic calculations.
Exact documents order imports and stock synchronisation, supporting the feasibility of connected order records.

assumptions: This typical workflow uses separate order and shipment records, with a spreadsheet joining them.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
Existing reporting configuration is checked before custom code is built.
Access is limited to necessary order data under GDPR; national consultation rules apply if employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Whether the existing {ERP} already provides the required report.
Availability of stable order identifiers and scheduled exports.
Agreed definitions for cancellations, returns, overdue orders and reporting cut-offs.
Who may publish management figures and access customer-level detail.
research_questions: Which reconciliation checks detect duplicate lines and missing shipments?
Can an approved shared snapshot satisfy management's reporting needs?
new_work: Review reconciliation exceptions and unexplained changes.
Maintain metric definitions, reporting calendars and access permissions.
Monitor failed refreshes and preserve approved report versions.
tasks.statement: Calculate and compile order-related statistics, and prepare reports for management.
